tt41-unit: WP-17 specifiers and import maps: root-relative, relative, absolute and protocol-relative http(s) specifiers are proxied with the module-graph segment; bare, data:, blob: and already-proxied ones are not; an import map's URL-like KEYS and every address are proxied the same way (so a rewritten specifier still prefix-matches a rewritten key), bare keys stay, scopes are mapped, "integrity" is dropped, malformed JSON is untouched

tt41-unit: WP-17 / WP-19 HTML wiring: an inline module's specifiers and import.meta.url are rewritten (a classic inline script's dynamic import too, without import.meta), an inline import map is rewritten, a body the HTML parser split at a "</script>" inside a string is left unchanged, crossorigin elements / module scripts / modulepreload carry the CORS segment (":i" for use-credentials), and an iframe names its parent document (":f") while links and forms stay plain navigations

tt41-unit: WP-17 root import map: a document with an id gets an import map routing run-time ROOT-RELATIVE module URLs ("/" → the site's root through the proxy, "/api/wp/s/" → itself so proxied URLs are untouched), injected right after the runtime when the page has none, MERGED into the page's own first map when it has one (one map per document, the page's own "/" key wins), using the final <base> origin; documents without an id get none

e2e-tt41: WP-18 oracle: Response.url / redirected / type after redirects, XHR responseURL, Request.url (fragment kept), redirect TAINT (A→B→C: C sees Origin "null" and must allow "null"; A→B→A: no same-origin cookies, needs CORS), mode "same-origin" leaving the origin fails, the full page URL as same-origin Referer, a classic worker's importScripts + Response.url, and a data: worker's opaque origin — the page's view AND what A / B / C saw are IDENTICAL natively and through the proxy

tt41-unit: WP-18 segments: every legal flag combination round-trips through parseSidSegment / flagString / decodeTarget in canonical order; out-of-order, repeated or unknown flags, a flag on "r" / "f", and a short document id are all rejected

tt41-unit: WP-18 redirect chains (Fetch §4.4 / §4.1): A→B→C taints the origin (Origin "null") and marks the chain cross-origin and cross-site; A→B→A taints too and keeps the request non-same-origin (no same-origin cookies, origin-only Referer, Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site); A→A stays clean; flags are sticky (never cleared by a later hop); mode same-origin refuses the cross-origin hop

e2e-tt41: WP-19 oracle: a CROSS-SITE iframe (B in A) — its navigation, its own image and its same-origin fetch get only SameSite=None cookies, and its Set-Cookie may store only SameSite=None; a SAME-SITE iframe (A′ in A) keeps every cookie and may store Lax — identical natively and through the proxy, including Sec-Fetch-Site and Referer

e2e-tt41: WP-17/18/19 adversary: page fetch() of a module gets its bytes UNCHANGED (only script / worker destinations are rewritten); a module the lexer cannot tokenise (an unterminated template) is served unchanged and labelled; an "f" (frame) tag on an image is not honoured as a frame (no frame-tree cookies, the script rules apply: none cross-site); chain flags only ever REMOVE — a tag without them is what the shim emits, so a page cannot claim more

e2e-tt42: WP-19 srcdoc frames (TT41 blocker): a STATIC srcdoc (server-rewritten: its image, its script's fetch, its inline MODULE's root-relative import, and a NESTED srcdoc's image) and DYNAMIC srcdoc set by script through the property and through setAttribute (shim-rewritten in an inert DOMParser document, runtime injected) — every resource reaches the site and every value the frames report to their parent is IDENTICAL natively and through the proxy

tt41-unit: WP-19 frame tree: a document registered with cross-site ancestors (xs) keeps that through the LRU; its subresources and script requests are cross-site for SameSite even to its OWN origin, while Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin still follow the document's origin; documentCsp drops frame-ancestors only for a validated nested frame

e2e-tt42: WP-20 oracle: computed dynamic import() — root-relative in the document AND in a module worker (where no import map applies), a colon in the first path segment (document and worker), an absolute CROSS-ORIGIN URL object (document and worker; CSP refuses the raw URL), new URL("./x", import.meta.url), a template, a relative computed path in the worker, a bare name routed by the page's map, a missing module (same rejection), a classic inline script's computed import, and an eval'd import() routed only by an import-map SCOPE — every value IDENTICAL natively and through the proxy

tt42-unit: WP-20 wrapper value semantics: for 20 run-time specifier values (root-relative, ./, ../, a colon in the first path segment, absolute http(s), protocol-relative, URL objects, an object with toString, credentials in the URL, bare names, data:, blob:, already-proxied, a non-http scheme, an unparseable string) the inline wrapper yields EXACTLY what the static rewriter yields for the same literal (or the string itself where the static rewriter leaves it); a throwing toString / a Symbol is passed through untouched so import() rejects natively

tt42-unit: WP-20 lexer: the first argument of every computed dynamic import is found with exactly acorn's source range — 19 shapes incl. nested templates, commas inside calls / arrays / objects, comments, a trailing comma, nested imports (literal inside computed, computed inside computed), import.source / import.defer — and literal imports, object / class METHODS named import and member calls are never wrapped

tt42-unit: WP-20 executed by V8: a rewritten script's import() calls receive the proxied address of every computed root-relative / relative / absolute / colon-segment / URL-object specifier, bare names unchanged, a literal import proxied statically, options still passed — and the original script, run the same way, receives the raw values (the difference is ONLY the proxying)

tt42-unit: WP-20 fail-safe and scope: a file the lexer cannot read is returned byte-identical (nothing wrapped); an `import(x)` followed by "{" on the next line is a call + block (ASI) at statement level and is wrapped (TT43; was TT42's documented miss), while the same shape inside an object literal / class body is a METHOD and stays untouched

tt43-unit: Modules (TT42 blocker `import(x)` + newline + `{` not wrapped): a computed import followed on the next line by "{" is a CALL then a block wherever only statements can stand (top level, blocks, function / method / arrow bodies, class static blocks, switch bodies), and a METHOD named import inside a class body (declaration or expression, with heritage) or an object literal (incl. `export default {`); acorn (MIT, test-only) is the oracle for every case — the exact computed ranges must match, and the rewritten source must still parse with the same number of import expressions

e2e-tt42: WP-21 browsers WITHOUT Fetch Metadata (TT41 blocker; emulated at the HTTP layer: real Chromium behind a front that removes every Sec-Fetch-* header, as Safari < 16.4 sends none): the destination is inferred from the URL tag + Accept — module scripts and module workers are still rewritten (all computed / static imports identical to native), a page fetch() of a module still gets its bytes UNCHANGED (the shim's "e" flag = destination empty), and a page fetch() of a document gets NO navigation secret (before TT42 every untagged request without Fetch Metadata counted as a navigation)

tt42-unit: WP-21 destination inference without Fetch Metadata: Safari's real Accept values (document / image / stylesheet / */*) and the URL tag decide — untagged document → navigate, untagged image / css → no-cors image / style, a markup-subresource tag → its Accept or script, a script tag → script (CORS) or, with the shim's "e" flag, empty (fetch / XHR), a frame tag → iframe; ANY Fetch Metadata header present → null (the browser's own values win); "e" round-trips in canonical order after "n", is rejected out of order, and survives a redirect hop

e2e-tt43: WP-22 oracle: SharedWorker shared like Chromium's own — two tabs of one profile (Fusion split view, one proxy session) and their nested same-site frames reach ONE worker (count and connections continue across them), a tab of another session gets its own; self.name, self.location, the worker's cookie jar (cookies set by BOTH tabs of the profile, only the other tab's in the other session), a second named worker, SecurityError for another site's script, SyntaxError for a bad URL and the error event of a missing script — every value IDENTICAL natively and through the proxy

e2e-tt43: WP-22 hosts and lifecycle (proxied): one hidden host document per (session, site) — opaque origin, sandboxed — and when the last page of a session leaves the site its host is removed (after the grace), while the other session's worker keeps its state; coming back starts a fresh worker

e2e-tt43: WP-22 attacks (proxied): a page that forges a connect with a document id the server never issued, or names another site's script, gets an error and no worker; a proxied page calling the broker's server endpoints directly (__shared-who / __shared-host) cannot read them, and the server refuses such requests (403: only the Fusion window may), so it can neither learn about documents nor mint host documents

tt43-unit: WP-22 sharing scope: two documents of one site in ONE session (two tabs of a profile) get ONE host and ONE worker key, and both pages' ports arrive there entangled (a message posted by each page is received at the host end); another session, another site, another name or a module type get their own; a hello is answered; the host gets nothing before it is ready, then everything in order

tt43-unit: WP-22 forged and malformed requests: a sender that is not an opaque-origin document is ignored; an unknown (session, document) — a forged or evicted id — is refused with an error and its port closed; a script on ANOTHER site than the server's record of the document is refused (a page cannot join another site's worker by claiming it); bad id / type / missing port refused; nothing is framed for any of them

tt43-unit: WP-22 partitioning: documents whose frame ancestors are cross-site (third-party contexts) never share with first-party documents of the same site, nor with each other (stricter than Chromium's per-top-site partition — disclosed); the server is asked once per document, not per connection

tt43-unit: WP-22 lifetime (HTML 'permissible worker'): the worker lives while any document is connected; the last pagehide starts a grace period after which the host is told to terminate it and an empty host is removed; a reconnect within the grace keeps the SAME worker (no release); a window that is gone (closed) is swept; a bye from a different window cannot disconnect someone else; a bye that overtakes its own connect (pagehide during the server check) cancels it

tt43-unit: WP-22 errors: a worker error reported by a host reaches exactly the documents connected to THAT worker (by their own connection ids), not other workers' documents; a message from an unknown host key is ignored

tt43-unit: WP-22 liveness by acknowledgement (the TT43 repair: a pagehide message is not always delivered): the broker pings each connected window; the document now in it answers with the ids it owns — a navigated window's NEW document (answering without the old ids) releases them at once; a busy page that misses one ping keeps its worker; a window that never answers is dropped after exactly 3 missed pings; an answer with a wrong nonce or from another window changes nothing
